variants.headline: Party divides in two
variants.sub: A split in {party} has produced the new party {splinter}.
variants.body:
The party {party} has split, with {splinter} the new breakaway party. The division is an organisational fact, not a complete explanation of the differences behind it. In considering {target}, readers should distinguish the break itself from unreported motives, ideological labels or claims about the balance of parliamentary strength.

Workers deserve political organisations that take their interests seriously, whether those organisations stand together or apart. Working people's needs belong at the centre of this discussion, rather than outside its political argument.

variants.headline: A political organisation breaks apart
variants.sub: The new party {splinter} has broken away from {party}.
variants.body:
A split in {party} has produced the new party {splinter}. A party has split in two, making political organisation itself the subject of the news. The assessment of {target} should address that break without treating either part as the natural owner of principles this report does not specify.

Workers deserve political organisations that take their interests seriously, whether those organisations stand together or apart. Working people's needs belong at the centre of this discussion, rather than outside its political argument.

variants.headline: Unity gives way to a party split
variants.sub: The party {party} has split, with {splinter} the new breakaway party.
variants.body:
The new party {splinter} has broken away from {party}. That is the development established in {colony}. Readers considering {target} should not be asked to accept an invented account of the dispute or an electoral forecast as part of the factual report.

Workers deserve political organisations that take their interests seriously, whether those organisations stand together or apart. Working people's needs belong at the centre of this discussion, rather than outside its political argument.
